investigations.name: biogears-sbml-sepsis
investigations.title: Simulation core — one sepsis model, every engine: composed, ensembled, orchestrated, benchmarked
investigations.description: A guided tour of the simulation core's capabilities on one real model. The same BioGears sepsis core is run under interchangeable engines (BioGears C++, two exact SBML integrators — Tellurium and COPASI — a PyTorch surrogate, and a Rust execution backend) and used to demonstrate, each as a runnable artifact: COMPOSITION (study 01 — the same spec under three engines by one node swap), ENSEMBLES (study 02 — a severity × engine batch in one sweep), ORCHESTRATION/WORKFLOWS (study 03 — the four-verb API composes modules into a pipeline and hands an Antimony/SBML file between engines, and a Nextflow pipeline fans the real composite across a severity grid), PERFORMANCE & EXECUTION BACKENDS (study 04 — where the compute goes, a ~40,000× surrogate tier, and the same composite run under the Rust viva-core backend), and CO-SIMULATION (study 06 — two processes exchanging state every tick: the physiology engine coupled to a closed-loop antibiotic controller, with untreated/early/delayed arms), and EVIDENCE & ACCEPTANCE (study 07 — turning runs into traceable pass/fail/pending acceptance criteria). A fidelity backbone (study 05) keeps it honest: where the engines agree, and where they do not.
investigations.question:
How can a compositional simulation core support interchangeable physiological
models, systematic perturbation studies, scalable execution, mechanistic
comparison, dynamic intervention, and evidence-based scientific validation? Taking
one real model, the BioGears sepsis core, each is a runnable artifact:
  01 INTERCHANGEABILITY — which model properties are preserved when the
     implementation changes (BioGears C++, extracted SBML/Tellurium, surrogate)?
  02 ENSEMBLES — how do severity and physiological parameters drive progression
     toward shock?
  03 ORCHESTRATION — can registered modules form a reproducible investigation with
     no new integration code, including inside a Nextflow pipeline?
  04 SCALABLE EXECUTION — where does acceleration preserve useful predictions, and
     where does it fail? Includes the Rust viva-core backend.
  05 MECHANISTIC FIDELITY — what explains the inflammatory agreement and the
     hemodynamic divergence between engines?
  06 DYNAMIC COUPLING — can coupled physiology and treatment produce consistent
     intervention responses (untreated vs early vs delayed)?
  07 EVIDENCE & ACCEPTANCE — can the Workbench turn runs into traceable evidence
     with explicit pass / fail / pending acceptance criteria?
The showcase is about what the core lets scientists test, not only what software it
can execute — while staying honest about where the engines agree and where they do not.
investigations.hypothesis:
This is a capabilities demonstration, not a single hypothesis test. The claim is
that the simulation core already does all of the above on a real model, with each
capability shown by an artifact that runs. The one genuine hypothesis is in the
fidelity backbone (study 05): the SBML extraction reproduces the inflammation core
to within ~0.1% but diverges from the BioGears engine in the hemodynamic layer. That
is a real, measured result, and it keeps the demonstration credible.

investigations.name: simulation-core-contract
investigations.title: The simulation-core contract — model in, results + verification out
investigations.description: The simulation core reduced to its contract. Where the companion investigation (biogears-sbml-sepsis) demonstrates the core's capabilities one by one, this one shows the single interface they all sit behind: simulate(model, request) -> results + verification. Study 00 runs several models through that one interface — an SBML file under Tellurium, the same model cross-checked against COPASI, a different engine, and a registered composite — and shows each returns results plus a passing verification.
investigations.question:
What is the simulation core, in one interface? Can you hand it any model, ask it to
run under any engine, and get back both the results AND a verification that the run
can be trusted — through one common entry point, with no re-wrapping per caller?
investigations.hypothesis:
The simulation core is a single contract: simulate(model, request) -> results +
verification. A model (SBML/Antimony or a registered composite) goes in; the core
runs it under a swappable engine and returns the observables together with a
structured verification (ran, finite, physically admissible, and — on request —
cross-engine agreement).
